texts.facts: This application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashment of FIR in Criminal Proceedingss in Crime No. 12/2022, registered at Police Station Khandwa, District Khandwa for offence under Sections 498-A, 294, 323, 506, 34 of IPC and under Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act. 2. The applicant No. 1 is the husband, application No. 2 is father-in- law, applicant No. 3 is mother-in-law and applicant No. 4 is sister-in- law who is a spinster. 3. At the outset, counsel for applicants seeks permission of this Court to withdraw this application filed on behalf of applicant No. 1 namely Vaibhav Tiwari. 4. The application on behalf of applicant No. 1 is accordingly dismissed as withdrawn. It is the case of the prosecution that respondent No. 2 lodged an FIR on 08.08.2022 on the allegations that she has already lost her father and she got married to applicant No. 1 on 19.06.2019. After her marriage, she resided with her father-in-law, mother-in-law, husband and sister-in-law in Sagar for about 15 days. Immediately after the marriage, her husband started scolding that he has married her only for the purposes of social recognition as well as dowry. Although the mother and elder father of respondent No. 2, Doctor Munish Mishra are millionaires but they have not given a cash amount of Rs.25,00,000/- but they have given only a cash amount of Rs.2,51,000/- and also threatened that now she will see that how he will treat her. When this fact was narrated by respondent No. 2 to her father-in-law, mother-in- law and sister-in-law that applicant No. 1 is threatening in such a manner, then they also scolded that her elder father-in-law is running a very big hospital and they have performed the marriage only for the purposes of dowry and, therefore, she should bring an amount of Rs.25,00,000/- and whenever, a further demand is made she should bring the money. When she was residing in Dhana (Sagar) she was kept as a prisoner and she was not allowed to go outside the house. Even if any guest used to come, still she was not allowed to come in front of them. When she narrated the entire incident to her elder father-in-law Doctor Munish Mishra, then he also tried to convince the applicants. Thereafter, her husband took her to Ratnagiri where he is posted. The applicants No. 2, 3 and 4 were also there and again they made a demand of Rs.25,00,000/- and on that issue they mentally harassed her and also insisted that in case if money is not brought then they would remarry applicant No. 1. She resided in Ratnagiri for a period of two months but applicant No. 1 never performed his duties of husband and he always insisted that respondent No. 2 should remain away from him because he doesn't want any child. When this fact was narrated by her to her mother-in-law that her husband is not allowing her to sleep with him, then she also insisted that she should not insist her son for children and she should also not insist her husband for physical relationship. After going back to Ratnagiri, when she cleaned the house, then she found the cloths, sleepers, undergarments of various girls, therefore, she got an suspicion that her husband must be having relationship with some other lady. When she talked to her husband in that regard, then he started abusing her in the name of mother and sister and also assaulted her by fist and blows and forcibly sent her to Dhana (Sagar). After coming back to Dhana, when she narrated this incident to her brother-in-law, father-in-law and sister-in-law that she had recovered the cloths, sleepers and undergarments of another lady from the house of applicant No. 1 and enquired as to whether applicant No. 1 has any intimate relationship with any girl or not, then all of them started abusing him and also assaulted her by fist and blows and insisted that respondent No. 2 should remain silent and should bring an amount of Rs. 25,00,000/-. In case if she raises any voice, then she would be killed and nobody would come to know about her whereabouts. Her husband also used to threaten her that he would push her in front of running train. Because of social liabilities, respondent No. 2 was somehow tolerating the physical and mental cruelty with hope and belief that one day the behavior of in-laws would improve. She stayed along with her in-laws till 21.03.2021 and thereafter, because of her mental and physical cruelty, she came back to her parental home. When she was staying in Khandwa, she had made a complaint on 20.09.2021 with an intention to save her marital life and her husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law as well as younger brother-in-law had given an assurance in Mahila Police Station that they would keep the respondent No. 2 properly and accordingly, on 10.12.2021 she went back to Ratnagiri where the behavior of applicant No. 1 was rude and he was neither talking to her nor he was taking her to any place. When her mother inquired from applicant No. 1 that if he was not Vaibhav Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103244755/ 3 intending to improve his conduct then why they gave an assurance in the police station that they would keep respondent No.2 properly, then it was replied by the husband of respondent No. 2 that in order to get rid of police, he had given a false assurance. The marriage was performed because of dowry but he is in love with somebody else and he would marry her and in case if an amount of Rs. 25,00,000/- is brought, then he would also keep respondent No. 2 with him. Thereafter, on 19.12.2021, she came back to Khandwa along with her mother and since then she is residing in Khandwa. The applicants had tortoured her mentally and physically for want of dowry of Rs.25,00,000/-. 6. It is submitted by counsel for applicants that so far as applicants No. 2 and 3 are concerned, they are father-in-law and mother-in-law. 7. The Supreme Court in the case of Geeta Mehrotra and Another Vs, State of Uttar Pradesh and Another, reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741 has held Applicants No. 2 and 3 are the father-in-law and mother-in-law. It is alleged by respondent No. 2 that immediately after the marriage, her husband scolded her that an amount of Rs.25,00,000/- should have been given in cash, whereas; only Rs.2,51,000/- has been given and also extended a threat that now she would see that how she is kept by him. When this fact was told by respondents No. 2 and 3, then they also scolded that her elder father is having a big hospital and the marriage was performed only for the purposes of dowry and, therefore, respondent No. 2 should bring an Vaibhav Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103244755/ 4 amount of Rs.25,00,000/- and she should also continue to bring the amount as and when it was directed. It was also alleged that respondent No. 2 was kept in Dhana (Sagar) like a prisoner and she was not allowed to meet with any guest. 13. When she also made a complaint to applicants No. 2 and 3 about the fact that applicant No. 1 is not discharging his duties of husband and has not involved in physical relationship, then it was replied by applicant No. 3 that she should not insist her husband to have children and she should not sleep with her husband.
texts.arguments: that if FIR as it stands does not disclose specific allegation against the accused more so against the co-accused specifically in a matter arising out of matrimonial bickering, it would be clear abuse of legal and judicial process to mechanically send the named accused in the FIR to undergo the trial unless of course the FIR discloses specific allegations which would persuade the Court to take cognizance of the offence alleged against the relatives of the main accused who are prima facie not found to have indulged in physical and mental torture of the complainant wife. 8. It is further submitted that the Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar Alias Sonam and Others Vs. State of Bihar and Others, reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599 has held that where the allegations made against the parents-in-law are not specific and general and omnibus allegations were made, then the prosecution is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and accordingly referred to paragraph 18 of the judgment passed in the case of Kahkashan Kausar (supra). 9. Per contra, the petitioner is vehemently opposed by counsel for respondent No. 2, it is submitted that the Supreme Court in the case of Taramani Parakh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and Others reported in (2015) 11 SCC 260 has held that passing taunts by the parents-in- law is sufficient to prosecute them for offence under Section 498-A of IPC. 10. The counsel for the State has also supported the registration of offence against applicants No. 2, 3 and 4. 11.
